name: Polar
purpose: One-click Bitcoin and Lightning networks for local development and testing: regtest Bitcoin Core with LND, Core Lightning, Eclair, Taproot Assets and Lightning Terminal nodes, run as Docker containers from a desktop application.

maintenance.evidence: Polar v4.0.0 published on 2026-01-06; the repository was pushed on 2026-10-23.

platforms.other: macOS (dmg) and Linux (deb, AppImage, RPM); the networks it builds run in Docker.

interfaces.description: Desktop application that builds and runs the networks.

nodeCompatibility: Its own regtest Bitcoin Core and Lightning nodes in containers, separate from the user’s nodes.
networking: Containers on the local Docker network.
security: Regtest only, with containers of its own; Docker Desktop on Windows is a large dependency with its own security model.
integrationMechanisms: Launch the user’s own installation (not built)

feasibility.notes: A Windows installer exists, but it needs Docker Desktop, which BTCortex does not install (zero-touch).

unverifiedClaims: The Windows installer’s architecture and signing were not checked.

name: Nigiri
purpose: Command-line tool for a regtest development environment in Docker Compose: Bitcoin Core in regtest, electrs and the Esplora explorer, Chopsticks (an HTTP proxy with a faucet and automatic blocks), and optionally Liquid, Lightning and Ark.

maintenance.evidence: v0.5.17 published on 2026-05-13; the repository was pushed on 2026-07-10.

platforms.other: The README strongly encourages WSL on Windows; Docker is required.

interfaces.description: nigiri start (--liquid, --ln, --ark), nigiri faucet <address>, nigiri push <hex>, nigiri rpc <command>.
Esplora at http://localhost:5000; Chopsticks on port 3000 (3001 with --liquid).

nodeCompatibility: Its own regtest Bitcoin Core in a container.
security: Regtest only.

feasibility.notes: Needs Docker and, on Windows, WSL; BTCortex runs regtest nodes natively instead.

unverifiedClaims: The electrs port is not stated in the README.

name: Warnet
purpose: Launches Bitcoin networks with a chosen number of nodes and topology, optionally with a Lightning network and payment activity, to monitor and analyse emergent network behaviour, on a local or remote cluster.

maintenance.evidence: v1.1.20 published on 2026-02-28; the repository was pushed on 2026-09-20.

platforms.other: A local or remote cluster back end, chosen at set-up.

interfaces.description: warnet, which asks for its back end and checks it.

nodeCompatibility: Its own Bitcoin Core nodes, optionally with Lightning.
security: Test networks of its own.

feasibility.notes: Research tooling for network simulations, not for a user’s node.

unverifiedClaims: Which cluster back ends it supports, and whether it runs on Windows, are not stated in the README.

name: btcdeb
purpose: Bitcoin Script debugging utilities: btcdeb steps through a script showing the stack, and btcc compiles readable script to hex.

maintenance.evidence: The repository was pushed on 2026-07-26; its latest tag is v5.0.24, from 2023.

platforms.other: Built from source on Linux or macOS (autogen, configure, make); a Docker build and an Emscripten (JavaScript) build.

security: Offline tool.

feasibility.notes: A developer tool without Windows builds.

unverifiedClaims: The exact date of v5.0.24 (2023) and Taproot support were not checked.

name: SimLN
purpose: Generates realistic payment activity on a Lightning network: on nodes the user controls (LND, Core Lightning, Eclair, LDK Server) or on a simulated network defined in a file.

maintenance.evidence: v0.2.5 published on 2025-06-24; the repository was pushed on 2026-09-16.

interfaces.description: sim.json with node credentials (certificates and macaroons, keys or API credentials) or a sim_network topology.

nodeCompatibility: LND, Core Lightning, Eclair and LDK Server, with keysend enabled.

dependencies.notes: Nodes to drive, unless the network is simulated.

security: It sends real payments from the nodes it is given; the README warns that paying destinations outside the user’s own nodes can drain liquidity and suggests signets and test environments.

feasibility.notes: A testing tool that spends from the nodes it controls.

unverifiedClaims: The binary name sim-cli and Windows support were not checked.

name: Mutinynet
purpose: Public Bitcoin signet for developers, with a mempool explorer (mutinynet.com) and a faucet (faucet.mutinynet.com) that sends on-chain coins, pays Lightning invoices and opens channels.

maintenance.evidence: The explorer and the faucet answered on 2026-10-23.

platforms.other: A public network with web services.

interfaces.description: Faucet with an OpenAPI description (faucet.mutinynet.com/openapi.json): up to 1,000,000 sats per request, on chain or over Lightning, and channel opening to the user’s node.

nodeCompatibility: A signet of its own; joining it needs its signet parameters, which its pages do not show.
security: Test coins with no value.

feasibility.notes: BTCortex sets up the default signet and testnet4, not custom signets.

notes: Public faucets for the default signet and testnet4 were not researched.
unverifiedClaims: Its block interval, signet challenge and whether it needs a modified Bitcoin Core were not checked.
